page: Amazon Web Services i8g.metal-48xl is a storage-optimized bare-metal server powered by AWS Graviton processors. It features 192 dedicated physical ARMv9 cores based on the Neoverse-V2 architecture, running at a clock speed of 2.8 GHz with a single thread per core. The system is equipped with 1536.0 GB of DDR5 memory, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per physical core. For high-capacity local storage, the instance includes 45,000 GB of NVMe SSD capacity. Network connectivity is delivered via a 100 Gbps baseline interface.

In benchmark testing, the server demonstrates top-tier multi-core performance, particularly in memory bandwidth and database operations. The stress-ng multi-core CPU test and Geekbench multi-core benchmarks both register in the top 10% tier. Memory bandwidth tests for both cached small blocks and uncached large blocks also achieve top-tier status, alongside Redis SET operations which reach 347.98 million operations per second. Conversely, single-core performance and LLM text generation speeds are more modest, with single-core stress-ng and Geekbench scores landing in the average tier, and LLM text generation for small and medium models scoring in the lower percentiles.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ARMv9 architecture and high resource density offer a favorable profile for large-scale deployments that require massive local storage and high memory throughput without the overhead of hyperthreading. The server is highly suited for high-throughput database systems, large-scale Redis deployments, static web serving, and multi-threaded data processing workloads such as software compilation and decompression tasks.
